headline: Brent tops $92.71 on a 10th day of US-Iran strikes and a Kuwaiti tanker hit — PSX slips but doesn't panic.
summary: Brent crude jumped to $92.71 a barrel (+1.87%, a six-week high) on a tenth straight day of US strikes on Iran, a Kuwaiti tanker hit near the Strait of Hormuz, and Houthi threats to blockade Red Sea shipping. KSE-100 is down 670 points (-0.38%) to 175,463 by mid-morning — a much milder reaction than the 2-3.5% single-day drops the same Hormuz story triggered two weeks ago, suggesting some desensitization. Pricier oil widens Pakistan's import bill and pressures the rupee and reserves right before the July 27 SBP decision (a hold is priced in). E&P gets a direct tailwind; OMCs, autos, and cement absorb the cost pain. The desk stays cautious, leans toward energy and steady dividend payers, patient on cyclicals.

sectors.name: E&P
sectors.why: Brent above $92 on the 10th day of US-Iran strikes gives OGDC/PPL/MARI a direct price tailwind, though their own charts (RSI 35-42, below 20/50-day averages) show no fresh momentum trigger yet.

sectors.name: Banks
sectors.why: 97% of surveyed analysts expect the SBP to hold at 11.5% on July 27, keeping banks' funding-cost carry intact, but risk-off sentiment keeps foreign flows thin.

sectors.name: OMCs
sectors.why: Daily fuel-price adjustments, a current account that swung to deficit in FY26, and circular-debt risk compound as crude climbs — PSO absorbs margin pressure without E&P's offsetting upside.

sectors.name: Cement
sectors.why: Cement is energy-cost sensitive; a firmer oil bill and a soft rupee squeeze input costs just as DGKC and MLCF are already trading below their 20-day averages.

sectors.name: Fertilizer
sectors.why: Fertilizer demand is domestic and largely insulated from the oil/shipping story — a defensive tilt while Hormuz risk stays elevated.

sectors.name: Autos
sectors.why: Imported-input costs rise with the oil bill and a weaker rupee, while inflation-pressured demand already shows up in INDU's and AIRLINK's double-digit 20-day declines.

watchlist.angle: An OBV-accumulation trigger (Volume leads price) fired today — on BML's own history this strategy has won 97% of 89 trades (+5.1% net/trade, still 83% out-of-sample). Fundamentals back it up: cheap at 6.4x earnings with a 32% net margin. Commercial Banks should get some support from a widely-expected SBP rate hold on July 27.
watchlist.risk: A fresh leg down in the Hormuz story would drag banks broadly lower regardless of BML's own setup — its 1.3x beta means it moves more than the market both ways.

watchlist.angle: Dolmen City REIT's confirmed 6.6% final dividend has its book-closure buy-by dated for today (2026-07-22), and it tops the desk's predictability screen at 75.7/100 — a rental-income REIT with less direct exposure to the oil/shipping shock than cyclical names.
watchlist.risk: The dividend payout ratio runs over 100% of earnings, so it's barely covered; a soft year could force a cut, and the price typically adjusts down by the dividend amount once the book closes.

watchlist.angle: UBL's board meets today to approve Q2CY26 results and declare entitlements — its share-dealing closed period (since July 14) lifts today too. The stock is already in an uptrend (+8.3% over 20 sessions, above both its 20- and 50-day averages) and ranks in the desk's top-10 predictability screen.
watchlist.risk: A results miss or a disappointing entitlement could reverse the recent run — and as an 8.3%-weight index heavyweight, UBL is also just along for the ride on any broader oil-driven risk-off day.

watchlist.angle: TPLT triggered a Donchian-55 breakout today — a strategy that's won 62% of past trades on the name (+3.6% net/trade, 75% hit rate out-of-sample), and Technology & Communication is one of the less directly oil-exposed sectors on the board.
watchlist.risk: The fundamentals card flags TPLT as currently lossmaking — a breakout on a loss-making small-cap (Rs5.4bn market cap, 1.3x beta) is exactly the kind of setup that reverses fast if the broader tape turns risk-off again.

catalysts.event: UBL board meeting — Q2CY26 results & entitlements
BWCL and HABSM board meetings scheduled
SBP MPC — first FY27 rate decision; a hold at 11.5% is widely expected

risks: Conflict escalation: a 10th day of US strikes on Iran, a Kuwaiti tanker hit near Hormuz, and Houthi threats to blockade Red Sea shipping could keep pushing Brent higher, deepening import-bill and rupee pressure.
SBP reserves already fell to $17.2bn (from $18.47bn) on debt repayments; a further drawdown into the July 27 MPC would hit sentiment hard.
Pakistan's current account swung to a small FY26 deficit (June alone -$649mn) after a run of surpluses — a worse read would compound oil-driven external-account stress.
